catalogue.name: Standard Product Delivery
catalogue.description: Idea to shipped, watched software. The full path, with gates where money and production are involved.

spec.objective: Ship working, watched software. The panel's PRD is the build brief: it is handed straight to an engineering agent, so it must be specific enough to implement and to test against.

directive.title: What should it do?
directive.description: Who it is for and what a person can do with it, in two or three sentences. The panel argues from this text and its PRD is the build brief, so a thin brief produces a thin product.
examples: A shift-swap board where staff offer a shift they cannot work, colleagues claim it, and the manager approves the swap. Used on a phone, mid-shift.

catalogue.name: Incident Response
catalogue.description: An app's alert fired. Investigate, fix the root cause with a regression test, have someone approve the release, ship it, and prove recovery from the monitor.

spec.objective: An app BOSS deployed is failing in front of users, and its own monitor raised the alarm. Find the root cause from the evidence — the app's metrics, its logs and the release that was serving — fix exactly that with a regression test that fails on the faulty release, and restore service. A person approves the release; recovery is judged by BOSS's monitor, not by the fix's author. If the evidence does not support a root cause, say so and stop rather than guess.

incident_id.description: The incident to respond to (Observability › the app's alert). An alert rule starts this for you when its Respond automatically is on (the app's Alerts tab).

catalogue.name: Incremental Build
catalogue.description: Builds the basics first, deploys them, then improves in steps.

spec.objective: Ship the app in visible increments: the basics live first, then improved in steps. The PRD MUST end with an increment plan, headed exactly '## Increment 1', '## Increment 2', … — at most 4 increments. Increment 1 is the core of the brief (the smallest app a person can use end to end); each later increment is a small set of the remaining requirements, in the order they add the most. Each build builds only its own increment, on the branch the earlier ones left.

directive.title: What should it do?
directive.description: Who it is for and what a person can do with it. The panel splits it into increments: the basics go live first, the rest arrive in steps.
examples: A lunch poll for a team: anyone proposes places, everyone votes once, the poll closes at 11:30 and shows the winner. Later: recurring polls, dietary tags and a Slack reminder.

catalogue.name: Scan for Business Rules
catalogue.description: Read an area or package of the code and propose the business rules it enforces, with the lines that prove them. A person approves each rule.

spec.objective: Find the business rules this part of the code enforces — validations, calculations, limits, state transitions, who may do what — and propose each one with the lines that enforce it. Propose only what the code shows; a person decides which rules are true. Nothing is built or changed.

scope.description: Areas, packages, classes, files or folders: a key from the Graph's project tree (area:<repo>:<area>, pkg:<repo>:<area>:<package>, module:<repo>:<package>, a class's symbol: key, file:<repo>:<path>) or a plain repository path to a file or folder. Checked when the scan starts. Start the scan from the tree to have this filled in.

directive.description: The scan proposes every business rule it finds in the scope. Name what matters most to you and the agent reads for that first.

catalogue.description: Read a document's clauses and propose the rule or code that implements each, or a gap when nothing does. A person reviews every proposal.

spec.objective: For each clause of the named document, find what already implements it — a business rule or a piece of code — and propose that link with a short rationale. A clause nothing implements is a gap, a valid and expected outcome, not an error. Nothing proposed here is approved automatically.

directive.title: What should the trace focus on? (optional)

catalogue.name: KG Investigation Pipeline
catalogue.description: Enrich a case's subject node from the Context Graph, match it against prior incidents, have an agent analyse the evidence, then remediate each finding family under human approval.

inputs.instructions: Read the Context Enrichment and Historical Pattern evidence for this subject. Cite the evidence for each finding, with a confidence, and group findings into families for remediation.
Route each finding family from Analysis to its own remediation lane.
Propose the remediation for this finding family, citing the evidence it is based on.

steps.question: Approve the proposed remediations for execution?
steps.guidance: Each remediation cites the evidence Analysis and the lanes assembled; nothing here has been executed yet.

inputs.instructions: Record this investigation's resolution as a precedent, so a later investigation's Historical Pattern step finds it.

spec.objective: Investigate the named subject node: assemble its connected rules, code, systems, owners and reports (Context Enrichment) and the incidents or precedents it resembles (Historical Pattern) — both $0 graph queries, never a model call. Analyse the assembled evidence and cite it; ask for one more enrichment round, at most twice, when the evidence is insufficient. Route each finding family to its own remediation lane, and execute nothing without a person's approval. Closure records what was found as a precedent, so the next investigation finds it too.

directive.title: What should this investigation focus on? (optional)
directive.description: Context Enrichment and Historical Pattern read the subject node's own graph; say what matters most and Analysis reads for that first.
examples: Check whether the connected repayment code and any prior incidents already cover crediting payments as of the date of receipt.

subject_id.title: Subject node
subject_id.description: The case's subject node to investigate (Graph › Knowledge Graph) — a clause, an incident, or whatever this case is about.

max_hops.title: Hops to enrich (optional)
max_hops.description: How far Context Enrichment walks from the subject node. Default 2.

catalogue.name: Banking Regulatory Compliance
catalogue.description: Trace a pasted regulation clause to the code and prior incidents that show whether it is already handled, confirm each finding against the code, and propose a remediation under a compliance officer's approval.

steps.question: Approve the proposed remediation package for execution?
steps.guidance: The remediation cites the evidence Compliance Assessment and the lane confirmation assembled; nothing has been executed yet. Approving triggers a scoped code-change task; it does not merge it.

inputs.instructions: Carry out the approved remediation package as a code task on the target repository.

spec.objective: For each clause of the named regulation document, open a compliance case and assemble what the graph already knows about it — connected business rules, code, systems, owners and reports (Context Enrichment), and the incidents or precedents it resembles (Historical Pattern) — both $0 graph queries. Assess the evidence as implemented, partly implemented or a gap, with a confidence and a citation, citing a correlated incident's detail where one was found. Route the finding to its family's lane, confirm it against the code, and propose a remediation package. Nothing executes without the Compliance Officer's approval. Closure records the resolution as a precedent, so the next investigation finds it too.

document_id.title: Document (optional)
document_id.description: The document to trace (Graph › Knowledge Graph › Documents). Leave blank and the trace reports nothing to do — add a document first.

subject_id.title: Subject node
subject_id.description: The case's subject node to investigate (Graph › Knowledge Graph) — a clause, an incident, or whatever this case is about.

directive.title: What should this compliance check focus on? (optional)
directive.description: Context Enrichment and Historical Pattern read the clause's own graph; say what matters most and the Compliance Assessment reads for that first.
examples: Check whether the connected repayment code and INC-2088's incident already cover crediting payments interest-first.

max_hops.title: Hops to enrich (optional)
max_hops.description: How far Context Enrichment walks from the subject node. Default 2.

symptom.title: What went wrong (optional)
symptom.description: A short description of the compliance gap or incident this investigation closes, for the precedent it records.
examples: Payment misapplied to principal instead of interest-then-principal order

cause_summary.title: Root cause (optional)
cause_summary.description: Why it happened, for the precedent a later investigation's Historical Pattern step will find.

execution_state.title: Execution state (optional)
execution_state.description: Whether the remediation's code task has been merged yet — the run finishing is not the same as the fix shipping.
